chunks: Ali, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
I asked him about a free man who had a slave girl under his ownership. He divorced her with an irrevocable divorce, then bought her. Is it permissible for him to copulate with her? He said: No.
ai.seo_question: Can a man marry his slave girl if he divorced her and then bought her back?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the fiqh of 'ikrah' (compulsion) in marriage by establishing that an irrevocable divorce (ba'in) severs the marital bond even if the husband repurchases the slave, preventing him from remarrying her without a new contract. It highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on the distinct legal status of slave women compared to free women, where the mechanism of divorce and repurchase does not automatically restore the previous marital union. This ruling underscores the importance of clear contractual intent in Islamic jurisprudence regarding concubinage and marriage.

en.hubeali:
Ali, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al Halby, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘

I asked him<sup>asws</sup> about a free man who had a slave girl under him. So he divorced her with an irrevocable divorce, then bought her. Is it Permissible for him that he copulates with her?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘No’.
